story.title: Customer submits checkout, system reserves stock and creates awaiting-payment order

test_cases.scenario_ref: Successful checkout reserves stock and creates order in awaiting-payment

expected_assertions.description: P1.stock_available transitions 5 -> 3 (delta -2)
P1.stock_reserved increases by 2
exactly one order row created with status='awaiting-payment' and grand_total matching server recompute
order_number matches /^ORD-\d{8}-\d{6}$/ and is unique across the orders table (no collision)
order_line snapshot captures price/name/SKU/quantity at submit time; later mutation of product row does NOT mutate the snapshot
audit_sink contains exactly one 'order.created' event with all 7 standard audit fields (event, actor, ts, before, after, reason, idem_key) populated per AP-Q12
response body does NOT include password, session_token, full shipping_address line, or phone — only references customer_id and order_number

test_cases.scenario_ref: Race-resolution on last unit — only one customer wins

expected_assertions.description: exactly one of {O_C1, O_C2} exists with status='awaiting-payment'; the other does not exist (no order row for the loser)
the losing customer receives a structured error code referencing P1 by id (per error_envelope TL dep); error message localized: 'สินค้าหมดในขั้นตอนยืนยัน'
P1.stock_available >= 0 at every observed step (no negative reading); no oversell
P1.stock_reserved + P1.stock_available + P1.stock_sold == initial total across the race window (conservation)
the losing customer's error response does NOT leak the winning customer's name, email, phone, shipping_address, customer_id, or order_number
audit_sink contains exactly one 'order.created' event for the winner and one 'checkout.rejected' or equivalent error event for the loser

test_cases.scenario_ref: Idempotent submit against double-click produces one order

expected_assertions.description: first submit with idempotency_key='ik-chk-001' creates order O123; second submit with SAME key and SAME body returns 200 with order_id=O123 and does NOT insert a new row
P1.stock_reserved equals 2 (single-reservation value) after replay — NOT doubled to 4
second submit response body is byte-for-byte equal to first response (order_id, order_number, grand_total, status all identical)
third submit with SAME idempotency_key='ik-chk-001' but DIFFERENT body (e.g. address changed) returns HTTP 409 with structured error code='idempotency_violation'
across the three calls, exactly one 'order.created' audit event is emitted; the 409 emits an 'idempotency_violation' audit event with idem_key='ik-chk-001'

test_cases.scenario_ref: Order creation emits audit event with required payload

expected_assertions.description: audit_sink contains exactly one event with all 7 standard fields enumerated (AP-Q12): (1) event=='order.created', (2) actor=='customer:C1' (uses customer_id surrogate, never email), (3) ts is valid ISO-8601 within +/-2s of submit time, (4) before==null, (5) after=={order_id:<uuid>, grand_total:<int>}, (6) reason=='checkout_submit', (7) idem_key matches request header
audit payload does NOT contain any of: password, session_token, card_number, PAN, CVV, full shipping_address line, phone, email, or name (forbidden-fields allow-list scan)
audit event is durably written before the API response is returned (write-before-respond invariant) — assert via audit_sink commit-timestamp < response_timestamp

test_cases.scenario_ref: Address from another customer is rejected

expected_assertions.description: HTTP 403 (or domain error_code='address_not_owned') returned when C1 references address A owned by C2
no order row created; no stock reservation taken; no notification emitted
audit event 'authz_denied' emitted with actor='customer:C1', resource='address:A', reason='cross_owner_access', and 7 standard fields populated
the 403 error response does NOT leak C2's shipping_address, name, phone, email, or customer_id — only that the address is not accessible

test_cases.scenario_ref: banking_grade_reversibility — payment failure releases stock reservation

expected_assertions.description: on payment_failure signal, stock_reserved is decremented by 2 and stock_available is restored to pre-checkout value (no reservation leak)
order transitions awaiting-payment -> payment-failed; no order row leaks in awaiting-payment state indefinitely
audit event 'order.payment_failed' emitted with before.status='awaiting-payment', after.status='payment-failed', reason='psp_decline'
stock_available + stock_reserved + stock_sold conservation holds across the reversal

test_cases.scenario_ref: banking_grade_reversibility — reservation TTL expiry releases stock

expected_assertions.description: at T+10min (TTL boundary), reservation still held; at T+11min (TTL expired) after sweep, order transitions to 'payment-timeout' and stock_reserved decrements by 2
stock_available restored to original pre-checkout value
audit event 'order.payment_timeout' emitted with reason='reservation_ttl_expired'
customer resubmit of the same cart after TTL expiry must re-acquire reservation (new order, new idempotency-key, new audit event) — the expired-reservation does not block a fresh submit
exactly 3 orders created in awaiting-payment; remaining 2 customers receive structured error_code='out_of_stock_at_confirm'
P1.stock_available reaches 0 (not negative) at end of race
no customer-PII fields (name, phone, email, shipping_address) of winners leak across error responses to losers
exactly 3 'order.created' audit events; exactly 2 'checkout.rejected' events

test_cases.scenario_ref: Server re-validates coupon at submit (consistency with story-2)

expected_assertions.description: submit fails with structured error_code='coupon_expired' or 'coupon_invalid_at_confirm' (per error_envelope TL dep)
no order row created; no stock reservation taken; no audit 'order.created' event emitted
audit event 'checkout.rejected' emitted with reason='coupon_expired' and idem_key populated
100 sequential order_number values all match /^ORD-\d{8}-\d{6}$/ and are pairwise distinct
consecutive order_numbers MUST NOT form a tight sequential counter visible to client (OQ-05 unresolved: assert either gaps >1 in >=5% of consecutive pairs OR random 6-digit suffix distribution)

test_cases.scenario_ref: banking_grade_idempotency — concurrent replay race (same key submitted twice in parallel)

expected_assertions.description: two parallel barrier-synced submits with the same idempotency_key='ik-chk-001' and same body produce exactly ONE order row; the second call returns the cached result of the first
P1.stock_reserved equals 2 (single reservation), NOT 4 — no double-reserve under concurrent replay
both responses contain the same order_id and order_number
exactly one 'order.created' audit event across the two concurrent calls; the cached-replay call emits an 'idempotency.replay_hit' observability event (not an audit duplicate)

test_cases.scenario_ref: banking_grade_authz — only cart owner can submit checkout (cross-tenant)

expected_assertions.description: customer C2's bearer token submitting checkout against C1's cart_id receives HTTP 403 (or domain error_code='cart_not_owned')
no order row created on C1's behalf; C1's cart state is unchanged; no stock reservation taken
audit event 'authz_denied' emitted with actor='customer:C2', resource='cart:<C1-cart-id>', reason='cross_owner_access'
the 403 response does NOT leak C1's name, email, phone, shipping_address, customer_id, or cart_contents

tl_design_dependencies.description: Canonical rule for computing the idempotency key from request fields. Required inputs: which fields participate (customer_id, cart_snapshot_hash, client-supplied nonce?), normalization (case, encoding, ordering), hash algorithm (sha256?), and server-side storage TTL. Without this, replay-safety tests cannot deterministically derive expected keys, anti-replay tests cannot scope key-namespace per customer, and NFR-reliab-001 cannot assert single-order invariant under PSP-timeout-driven retries.

Lock granularity for stock reservation: per-SKU row lock vs reservation-table advisory lock vs optimistic CAS; isolation level (read-committed / repeatable-read / serializable); timeout semantics; deadlock policy. Required so the deterministic concurrency harness (env-ci-race-deterministic) can wire lock-instrumentation probes and the race tests can assert lock-acquisition order and conservation invariants.

Standard error shape for payment/checkout failures: error code namespace, reason field, message-vs-code split, structured details, localization key (Thai/English). Required so error-path assertions reference stable codes ('out_of_stock_at_confirm', 'coupon_expired', 'address_not_owned', 'cart_not_owned', 'idempotency_violation') rather than brittle prose strings; also drives cross-test consistency.

JSON-Schema for audit events: the 7 standard fields (event, actor, ts, before, after, reason, idem_key) per AP-Q12 PLUS payment-specific extensions (provider_event_id, settlement_state, error_code) and a registered event-name vocabulary (order.created, order.payment_failed, order.payment_timeout, authz_denied, checkout.rejected, idempotency.replay_hit, idempotency_violation). Required so every audit_event assertion can validate against a canonical schema and forbidden-field allow-list checks are well-defined.
